saints.name: Sts. Louis and Zélie Martin
saints.title: Married Couple
saints.shortBlurb: The devout parents of St. Thérèse of Lisieux, the first spouses canonized together as a couple…
biography: Louis Martin, born at Bordeaux in 1823, had hoped to be a monk but, defeated by Latin, became a watchmaker; Marie-Azélie Guérin, born near Alençon in 1831, was refused by the Sisters of Charity and became a maker of Alençon lace. They married at Alençon on 13 July 1858, three months after meeting, and built a home of prayer and open-handed charity.

Of their nine children, four died young; the five daughters who grew up all entered religion — four as Carmelites at Lisieux, one a Visitandine at Caen — among them the youngest, Thérèse of the Child Jesus, canonized in 1925 and later a Doctor of the Church. Zélie's lace business prospered so well that in 1870 Louis sold his own shop to join her in it.

Zélie died of breast cancer at Alençon in 1877, aged forty-five, and Louis moved the family to Lisieux; in his last years he suffered strokes and mental decline, dying in 1894. Declared venerable in 1994 and beatified at Lisieux in 2008, they were canonized by Francis on 18 October 2015, the first spouses raised to the altars together, and are patrons of married couples, parents, and the sick.
saints.knownFor: Raising a saintly family and holiness in married life.
